FEP / OpenAI common mathematical coordinates

Positive authored feature assignments. Absence means not assigned, not logical negation. FEP rows are family unions; upstream rows are individually named result units. Hypothesis axes include stated premises and regimes, not a common proposition.

Each authored coordinate has unit weight. Domain/carrier/premise groups with more coordinates contribute more potential mismatches; no hidden group normalization.

Feature proximity creates no relation edge, equivalence witness, imported theorem, native evidence, or scientific promotion.

fep-001 · Variational Free Energy Bound · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-free-energy
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep001.FEP001.fep001_variationalUpperBound_eq_iff
Invariant
Surprisal plus Mathlib's native measure KL upper-bounds surprisal; for finite measures and finite surprisal, equality holds exactly when the approximate and exact posterior laws coincide.
Assumption review
The inequality is unconditional in ENNReal. Gap separation requires finite measures, and bound equality additionally requires surprisal below infinity so additive cancellation is sound.
Non-vacuity
Matching finite posterior laws attain equality, while any unequal finite pair has a nonzero KL gap and hence a strict finite-surprisal remainder.

fep-002 · Variational Evidence Bound via KL Divergence · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-free-energy
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep002.FEP002.fep002_vfe_ge_surprisal
Invariant
Variational free energy, defined as surprisal plus Mathlib KL divergence, upper-bounds surprisal and is exact at the posterior.
Assumption review
The bound is unconditional over measures in a measurable space; exactness uses Mathlib's SigmaFinite assumption for KL self-divergence. The codomain is ENNReal, so infinite divergences are represented without a finiteness side condition.
Non-vacuity
Any sigma-finite posterior supplies the equality witness q = posterior, while distinct measures can produce a nonzero or infinite KL remainder.

fep-003 · Discounted Pragmatic Cost · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-active-inference
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep003.FEP003.fep003_pragmaticCost_succ
Invariant
Finite-horizon pragmatic cost is the discounted ENNReal sum of stage costs; horizon extension exposes the exact terminal increment, costs are pointwise monotone, and horizon extension is monotone.
Assumption review
All costs and the discount live in ENNReal, so nonnegativity and infinity are represented directly. This is the pragmatic-cost input to EFE; epistemic value and its sign are owned by fep-021.
Non-vacuity
For positive discount and positive new stage cost, the terminal increment is nonzero; strict growth of the total additionally requires the previous accumulated cost to be finite. Discount zero at positive horizons exposes the zero-increment boundary.

      fep003_pragmaticCost discount stageCost horizon +
        discount ^ horizon * stageCost horizon

fep-004 · Finite Diagonal Fisher Metric · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-information-geometry
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep004.FEP004.fep004_fisherMetric_eq_zero_iff
Invariant
A finite diagonal Fisher metric is symmetric and positive semidefinite under nonnegative information weights, and becomes positive definite under strictly positive weights.
Assumption review
The information weights are explicit inputs rather than derived from a statistical family in this row. Positive definiteness requires every coordinate weight to be strictly positive; fep-038 computes the one-dimensional Bernoulli weight and the composed theorem identifies that specialization.
Non-vacuity
Any strictly positive nonconstant weight vector and nonzero tangent has positive norm, while the zero-characterization excludes every nonzero coordinate direction.

fep-017 · Posterior Kernel Reconstruction · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-bayesian-mechanics
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep017.FEP017.fep017_posterior_joint_reconstruction
Invariant
Mathlib's posterior is a Markov kernel whose composition with the predictive law reconstructs the swapped prior-likelihood joint law; for a Markov likelihood it also recovers the prior.
Assumption review
Conditional on standard-Borel and nonempty latent structure plus finite prior and likelihood kernel. The Radon--Nikodym Bayes formula additionally uses countability of the latent space and standard-Borel observation structure. This is a regular posterior-kernel theorem, not a claim about learned or approximate posteriors. The Bayes-density formula additionally assumes countable latent and nonempty standard-Borel observation structure and holds only almost everywhere under the predictive law. Every selected posterior fibre is normalized, including version choices at null observations.
Non-vacuity
Every posterior fibre has mass one, and the identity Markov kernel supplies a concrete prior-recovery witness; non-deterministic finite kernels exercise a nontrivial reconstructed joint law.

fep-020 · Two-State Markov Relaxation · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-bayesian-mechanics
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep020.FEP020.fep020_tendsto_uniform
Invariant
A normalized symmetric two-state transition has the uniform stationary law; its exact n-step deviation is (1-2α)^n times the initial deviation and converges to zero for 0 < α < 1.
Assumption review
Transition nonnegativity uses α in [0,1], while convergence uses the strict interior so |1-2α| < 1. This is an exact finite-state Markov relaxation model, not a discretized Langevin diffusion.
Non-vacuity
For α = 1/4 and any nonstationary initial mass, deviations contract geometrically by 1/2 at every step; at α = 1 the chain instead alternates and the strict-interior convergence premise excludes it.

Only support nonemptiness is required; inverse temperature and costs may be arbitrary reals. This proves an exact stochastic policy law but not optimality, sampling behavior, or a temperature limit.

fep-034 · Normalized Bayesian Filtering · formalized
Family context (editorial)
core-active-inference
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep034.FEP034.fep034_filter_joint_reconstruction
Invariant
A transition-composed predictive prior and native observation posterior reconstruct the swapped predicted-state/observation joint law, with probability mass one in every posterior fibre.
Assumption review
Conditional on standard-Borel nonempty latent structure, a finite prior, and finite transition and observation kernels; prediction preserves total mass when the transition is Markov, and posterior recovery additionally requires a Markov observation kernel. This is a one-step exact filter, not a convergence or learned-state theorem. Posterior normalization holds in every fibre of the selected Markov version; Bayes reconstruction identifies the version only relative to the predictive observation law, so no unique pointwise Bayes ratio at null observations is asserted.
Non-vacuity
A nonidentity finite Markov transition followed by a noisy observation kernel yields a nontrivial predictive prior and posterior; each posterior fibre has mass one rather than merely nonnegative unnormalized weight.

Assumption review
The finite sampling law requires p in [0,1]. Interiority uses the intrinsic count bound, and consistency transfer explicitly assumes convergence of the raw empirical frequency. Invariant
The differentiated Bernoulli family has zero expected score and Fisher information 1/(p(1-p)); its inverse metric defines a dual natural gradient. The supplied coordinate-Jacobian expression squares to Fisher information and factorizes the metric.
Assumption review
Metric positivity, inverse-metric duality and the coordinate-Jacobian algebra require 0 < p < 1. Identification of that supplied expression with the derivative of the authored 2*arcsin(sqrt p) coordinate requires the separately reviewed interior HasDerivAt bridge. No path-length theorem or general statistical manifold is asserted by the current topic declarations.

At p = 1/2 the Fisher information is 4, every nonzero tangent has positive metric norm, and the natural-gradient map rescales nonzero covectors by 1/4.

Mathlib's real Gaussian law is normalized with its stated mean and variance; the one-dimensional closed-form entropy is strictly variance-monotone, differentiable with derivative 1/(2v), and under v=κT has derivative 1/(2T) and heat capacity 1/2.
Assumption review
The native probability, mean, and variance theorems include the zero-variance Dirac boundary. Entropy monotonicity and derivatives require positive variance, and the thermal relation requires κ,T>0. For unit scale and positive temperature, the Gaussian law is nondegenerate, its entropy response is nonzero, and the dimensionless heat capacity is exactly 1/2.

Invariant
Fermat's theorem makes every local minimum critical; for an exact positive-curvature quadratic, the derivative is the stated gradient, the center is the unique critical point and global minimizer, and the scalar Hessian is strictly positive.
Assumption review
The general derivative-zero theorem uses Mathlib's local-minimum notion. Uniqueness and positive second derivative are proved only for the explicit scalar quadratic with a>0, not inferred for arbitrary differentiable objectives. The general deriv = 0 wrapper uses Mathlib's totalized derivative, which is zero also at nondifferentiable points; only the explicit quadratic HasDerivAt declarations establish differentiability here.
Non-vacuity
Every positive a and noncenter x has nonzero gradient and strictly larger energy than the center, while the Hessian 2a is nonzero everywhere.

For nonzero evidence, likelihood-times-prior masses have the Bernoulli mass-vector form at the updated parameter. A probability-law interpretation additionally requires a prior in [0,1], nonnegative likelihoods and positive evidence.
Assumption review
Closure is exact for a binary latent hypothesis and binary evidence likelihood. Interior prior and positive likelihood assumptions prove positive evidence and keep the updated parameter in [0,1]. This is a finite Bernoulli conjugate family, not Beta-density conjugacy.

Nonnegativity preservation requires nonnegative factors and inputs. Order monotonicity requires nonnegative factors and pointwise ordered inputs, which may themselves be negative. The native result assumes a finite prior, a finite likelihood kernel, a nonempty standard-Borel parameter space, countable generation between the parameter and observation spaces, and prior-almost-every likelihood domination. The countable specialization discharges domination but remains an almost-everywhere identity, not a pointwise formula on null observations.
Non-vacuity
Countable nonempty parameter spaces and finite Markov likelihoods instantiate the specialization without an authored domination proof; observations in a predictive null set remain intentionally unconstrained.

Family context (editorial)
control-and-planning-as-inference
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep071.FEP071.fep071_sophisticatedEFE_backward_step
Invariant
Finite sophisticated expected-free-energy recursion reoptimizes after each observation-dependent update, and a two-stage witness separates feedback from every fixed open-loop second action. Separately, under the explicit BayesianBeliefModel filter-soundness and full-support premises, the generative-model specialization agrees with the reachable-belief POMDP optimum; this stronger statement does not make the generic primary Bayesian.
Assumption review
Belief, action, and observation carriers are finite and Action is nonempty so each finite argmin exists. The theorem is a maintained finite-horizon recursion with an exact Boolean two-stage witness; it does not prove continuous-state or infinite-horizon sophisticated planning. SophisticatedEFEModel supplies a real stage objective and an observation-indexed update. This generic recursion does not certify Bayes correctness or derive the stage objective from mutual information. Reviewed 2026-10-23 in docs/relations-endpoint-adjudication.md (FORM-S11): FEP.PerceptionActionLoop.bayesSophisticatedValue_eq_pomdpOptimum and bayesRiskAmbiguity_eq_sophisticated provide the separate Bayesian specialization on a finite filter-closed indexed belief family with positive-evidence update soundness, nonempty actions, and full support at every indexed belief. boolBayes_rederives_feedbackWitness re-derives the ordinary Boolean mismatch-cost tree through the filter; it is not a full-support EFE witness. boolKeepPrior_not_bayesian and boolKeepPrior_agreement_fails expose the observation-ignoring update boundary. No null-observation Bayes identity, full-simplex enumeration, continuous-state or infinite-horizon result is claimed.
Non-vacuity
In the witness, false and true observations choose different continuation actions, and the resulting expected cost is strictly below that of either fixed Boolean continuation.

theorem fep071_sophisticatedEFE_backward_step
    (model : SophisticatedEFEModel Belief Action Observation)
    (horizon : ℕ) (belief : Belief) :
    sophisticatedEFEValue model (horizon + 1) belief =

        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief (sophisticatedEFEAction model horizon belief)

              (model.update belief (sophisticatedEFEAction model horizon belief)
                observation)

The state carrier is finite and the pointwise-product normalizer must be strictly positive. Disjoint supports are excluded. This unit-weight product uses exponents one, not the one-half exponents of an equal-weight logarithmic pool, and no externally Bayesian pooling property is claimed.

fep_fep114.FEP114.fep114_subGaussian_empiricalMean_tail
Invariant
A finite independent family with certified sub-Gaussian moment-generating functions satisfies the explicit exponential upper-tail bound for its summed empirical-mean event.
Assumption review
Observables are indexed by Fin sampleCount, are independent under the supplied measure, and each has a nonnegative sub-Gaussian proxy variance. Deviation is nonnegative. The theorem neither assumes IID data nor asserts an asymptotic law; a positive sample count is needed for the usual empirical-mean interpretation even though real division is totalized at zero.
Non-vacuity
Multiple independent nonconstant centered observables with positive proxy variances give a nontrivial exponentially decaying bound as deviation grows.

learning-concentration-and-model-evidence

fep_fep116.FEP116.fep116_finitePACBayes_with_confidence
Invariant
For any finite posterior, a Gibbs certificate whose potential is inverse temperature times the population-minus-empirical loss gap converts a certified log-MGF budget into an empirical-loss plus KL-complexity population-loss bound.
Assumption review
Hypotheses are finite; inverse temperature is positive; the Gibbs reference equals the prior and carries full support; confidence lies in (0,1); and the certificate log partition is bounded by log(confidence^-1). The theorem is deterministic conditional on this log-MGF premise and does not itself prove that the premise holds with high probability over data.
Non-vacuity
Unequal posterior and prior laws contribute a finite KL penalty, nonzero loss gaps enter through the certified potential, and smaller confidence increases the explicit log(confidence^-1) budget.

Invariant
For a positive finite sample, add-one smoothing decomposes forecast error into contracted empirical error plus an exact target-dependent offset.
Assumption review
The success count and sample count are natural numbers, sample count is positive, successes do not exceed it, and the target lies in the unit interval. The theorem is an algebraic identity, not a stochastic consistency or posterior-contraction result.
Non-vacuity
The shrinkage coefficient lies in the unit interval and the separate boundary witness in fep-122 shows that the offset can be nonzero.

Sample count is positive, each success count is bounded by it, and the target is in the unit interval. The factor-two inequality is conservative and finite-law expectation is not an asymptotic risk claim.
Non-vacuity
Nonzero empirical error and nonzero boundary offset both contribute to the integrated upper bound under a nondegenerate finite sampling law.

This is a strict-containment instance. Constant count1 gives both events empty despite distinct thresholds; event distinctness is not required by the theorem.

theorem fep128_policyTreeValue_node
    {Belief Action Observation : Type*}
    [Fintype Belief] [Fintype Action] [Fintype Observation]
    (model : PolicyTreeModel Belief Action Observation)
    {depth : ℕ} (action : Action)
    (continuation : Observation → PolicyTree Action Observation depth)
    (belief : Belief) :
    policyTreeValue (depth := depth + 1) model (action, continuation) belief =
      model.stageCost depth belief action +
        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief action observation *
            policyTreeValue model (continuation observation)
              (model.update belief action observation)

      model.stageCost depth belief action +
        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief action observation *
            policyTreeValue model (continuation observation)
              (model.update belief action observation)

fep_fep148.FEP148.fep148_meanParameter_strictMono
Invariant
Positive statistic variance throughout a closed interval makes the natural-to-mean coordinate map strictly monotone and injective there.
Assumption review
Variance positivity is an explicit interval premise. The theorem is local to a stated scalar interval and does not assert global dual-flat coordinates or positivity for degenerate statistics.
Non-vacuity

fep_fep156.FEP156.fep156_boltzmann_control_posterior_minimizes_efe
Invariant
On a finite policy carrier with fixed precision, the KL-regularized control objective (expected EFE plus inverse-precision KL to the prior) is minimized exactly by the Boltzmann control posterior proportional to prior * exp(-gamma * G); the minimized value is -gamma^-1 log Z, the EFE splits as risk plus ambiguity, and the finite and treewise argmin views agree.
Assumption review
The primary Boltzmann-law minimization assumes a normalized finite full-support prior and gamma>0 and minimizes expected supplied real cost plus gamma^-1 KL to the prior over normalized candidate laws. Identifying that cost with model-derived EFE is a separate specialization. Deterministic finite-policy and finite-tree EFE/risk-ambiguity argmin statements are separate declarations. No continuous-action or general planning algorithm is claimed; supported sparse-prior and negative/zero-precision boundaries remain separately scoped foundation results.
Non-vacuity
A full-support finite prior, positive precision and nonconstant finite cost give a nondegenerate Boltzmann probability law attaining the unique KL-regularized objective minimum -gamma^-1 log Z. Separately, a nonempty finite policy carrier has a deterministic EFE argmin and the treewise declarations preserve finite optimal values; that deterministic argmin is not identified with the Boltzmann law or its regularized objective value.

Family context (editorial)
standalone-efe-formalizations
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep157.FEP157.fep157_loop_invariant_surprisal_bound
Invariant
For one positive-evidence observation, outcome surprisal is bounded by perception VFE, whose exact gap is finite KL from the belief to its filtered posterior; the selected filtered-model policy has EFE equal to risk plus ambiguity under FullSupport. Supporting declarations give the finite observation-averaged posterior-KL chain bound, native predictive KL data processing, a Dobrushin total-variation bound under an explicit coefficient, Bayesian-filter/kernel reconstruction and selected-policy minimization. Flat policy EFE makes the policy posterior equal its prior. No realized-observation monotonicity, accumulated trajectory bound or dynamical fixed-point/convergence theorem is asserted.
Assumption review
Policy, state and outcome carriers are finite; beliefs are normalized laws on the finite state carrier, not an assumed finite space of all beliefs. The primary needs positive observation evidence and FullSupport at the filtered model; finite posterior-KL decomposition additionally needs a positive reference law and full likelihood support. The native predictive DPI is separately stated on discrete measurable carriers. Prediction uses an explicit HasDobrushinBound; strict TV contraction additionally needs a coefficient below one and a nonzero initial distance. The flat-EFE posterior identity is algebraic and is not an iterated-loop fixed-point theorem.
Non-vacuity
Nonuniform supported beliefs and informative likelihoods can instantiate the exact VFE gap and the observation-averaged KL decomposition. The selected-policy and filter/kernel equalities are actual finite operations. The flat-EFE case yields posterior=prior, an algebraic boundary; these declarations do not supply a strict realized-step surprisal-decrease or dynamical fixed-point witness.

Family context (editorial)
standalone-efe-formalizations
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep158.FEP158.fep158_reduction_free_energy_monotone
Invariant
Weights bounded above by one make positive unnormalized masked evidence no greater than full predictive evidence, so its negative-log evidence free energy is no smaller. For a nonnegative mask with positive prior normalizer, the normalized reduced-prior predictive equals maskedEvidence divided by that normalizer; no universal direction relative to full predictive evidence is claimed for this normalized quantity. Supported reduced posteriors obey exact weighted reconstruction and cross-multiplied odds identities. Separately, the Gibbs objective gap to its optimizer equals finite KL, and the fixed-variance Gaussian natural-chart log ratio is explicit.
Assumption review
Parameters and evidence use finite normalized law/kernel carriers. The primary free-energy comparison assumes weight<=1 pointwise and positive masked evidence. Normalized masked-prior/posterior statements additionally require nonnegative weights, positive prior mask normalizer and positive relevant evidence; ordinary log/ratio clauses retain their support assumptions. GibbsCertificate optimizer-gap identities and the fixed-variance Gaussian log Bayes factor are separate statements, with no general asymptotic model-selection or automatic full/reduced evidence monotonicity claim.
Non-vacuity
With prior masses(1/2,1/2), likelihoods(9/10,1/10) and mask(1,0), full evidence is1/2, unnormalized masked evidence9/20, mask normalizer1/2 and normalized reduced-prior evidence9/10. Positive support permits exact posterior reweighting. This exercises both evidence notions without reversing the proved comparison.

Family context (editorial)
standalone-efe-formalizations
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep159.FEP159.fep159_epistemic_gain_bounded_by_affinity
Invariant
For a full-support two-state belief, its finite KL gap to the invariant law is at most productionRate/decayRate. A specific policy-independent perfect-observation model has EFE equal to the semigroup-evolved gap; that gap is bounded by the explicit squared exponential relaxation factor times the initial chi-square expression. At positive time the supported source-target slice production equals(1-rho)*productionRate/decayRate. Under inverse-epsilon rate scaling, the old attainable-scale theorem is preserved. The uniform theorem controls every sufficiently small positive epsilon, and the Tendsto theorem proves the genuine right-hand limit at zero for every fixed positive time and initial finite law.
Assumption review
All statements use the explicit two-state continuous-time semigroup and positive rates. The uniform bound and right-hand limit require fixed strictly positive time but permit zero-mass atoms in the initial law. The affinity and slice-path identities retain their explicit full-support premises; the path identity is one-slice, not a general path-space theorem. The ness_flow import remains only an orphan-adoption marker.
Non-vacuity
A symmetric-rate nonstationary three-quarter/one-quarter belief and a sparse point mass both satisfy the positive-time right limit. The stationary law has exactly zero gap at every positive scale and nonnegative time. At time zero the symmetric point mass retains log 2 at every positive scale, so dropping the positive-time premise is refuted. These controls use the same existing finite probability carrier and public owner.

Family context (editorial)
standalone-efe-formalizations
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep160.FEP160.fep160_aoDecomposition
Invariant
On a finite state space with a full-support stationary law, every rate field decomposes exactly into a reversible part (detailed-balanced relative to the law) plus a circulation part (skew in the law-weighted sense); the stationary edge current equals twice the law-weighted circulation part, the reversible part carries no current, removing the circulation part is exactly detailed balance, the log-affinity splits into the Ao-potential drop plus the skew force, stationarity makes the node divergence of the stationary current vanish, and the directed three-cycle witness is stationary, divergence-free, and circulating.
Assumption review
All statements are finite-carrier algebra: the Ao potential is the pointwise -log p* mass field and is deliberately distinct from the thermodynamic Helmholtz free energy of fep-013; the continuum Fokker-Planck equation, a state-dependent diffusion matrix field, and SDE noise are not formalized. Stationarity and the probability current reuse the established FEP.ContinuousTimeMarkov generator contract.
Non-vacuity
The decomposition is unconditional for every rate field under the full-support hypothesis, and the directed three-cycle exhibits a genuine NESS whose circulation part is 1/2 at the forward edge.

fep-166 · Uniqueness of the Law-Weighted Reversible/Circulation Split · formalized
Family context (editorial)
standalone-efe-formalizations
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep166.FEP166.fep166_split_unique
Invariant
Any competing pair S, A with W = S + A, p-weighted reversibility of S and p-weighted skewness of A coincides pointwise with the canonical symmetricPart and circulationPart of the rate field; the reversible boundary is in uniqueness form (a p-reversible field has the split (W, 0)), and on the concrete two-state datum the constraint-satisfying split is the canonical one with genuinely nonzero forward circulation 1/2 and strictly negative reverse entry -1/4.
Assumption review
Positivity of the finite law is the only analytic input and licenses the divisions; no stationarity hypothesis, no generator contract, and no nonnegativity claim for the circulation part enter the statements.
Non-vacuity
The t-0060 datum with weight law p = (1/3, 2/3) and rate entries 1, 5/2, 3/4, and -1 satisfies every constraint clause, its split is forced to be the canonical one, and the circulation entries 1/2 and -1/4 are computed exactly, so the uniqueness characterization is exercised on nontrivial data.

fep-167 · Frobenius Least-Squares Projection of the Symmetrizer · formalized
Family context (editorial)
geometric-mechanics-notation
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep167.FEP167.fep167_frobenius_pythagoras
Invariant
For symmetric S the squared Frobenius norm splits exactly as ||H - S||^2 = ||H - symmetrize H||^2 + ||symmetrize H - S||^2, the symmetrizer minimizes the squared distance among symmetric matrices with equality exactly at the symmetrizer, the symmetric minimizer is unique, and the concrete nonsymmetric datum [[0,1],[0,0]] carries residual exactly 1/2.
Assumption review
Matrix projection only, no differentiability, no continuum Clairaut theorem, no Bregman-projection existence/uniqueness claim.
Non-vacuity
The residual example evaluates to exactly 1/2 on nonsymmetric data, and symmetric data attains the zero residual exactly at the symmetrizer, so both the strict and the degenerate boundary are realized.
Acceptance probe (requirement; not executed here)

fep-168 · Quantitative Control of the Uncanceled Divergence Remainder · formalized
Family context (editorial)
geometric-mechanics-notation
Primary qualified witness
fep_fep168.FEP168.fep168_weightedDivergence_eq_remainderDot
Invariant
On the fep-163 carrier the weighted divergence equals dot (divQ DQ) g under the cancellation hypotheses, the squared Cauchy-Schwarz budget (weightedDivergence)^2 <= (sum r_i^2)(sum g_i^2) bounds the uncanceled remainder with its abs-product corollary, and equality is attained on aligned nonzero data with norm(g)^2 = 1.
Assumption review
Quantitative budget on the fep-163 finite derivative-data carrier; the coupling hypothesis is sufficient-not-necessary (slot = dot(Qg, dlogp)); no PDE-discretization or entropy-production claim.
Non-vacuity
The aligned datum Q = [[0,1],[-1,0]], H = diag(1, 2), DQ with divQ (1, 0), and g = (1, 0) attains the budget with equality, while the pinned remainderG = (1, 1) datum is strict with gap 1, so both the equality and the strict boundary are realized.

fep-153fep-010formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep153_continuousDetailedBalance_extends_fep010

fep-158fep-117formalFEPComposed.fep158_masked_evidence_supplies_fep117_reduced_odds

fep-159fep-153formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep159_epistemicGain_extends_fep153_stationary

fep-160fep-025formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep160_aoNess_extends_fep025_current

fep-161fep-160formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep161_skewCancellation_extends_fep160_aoNess

fep-162fep-161formalFEPComposed.fep162_clairautSymmetrize_extends_fep161_skewCancellation

fep-164fep-025formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep164_graphCurrent_extends_fep025_current

fep-165fep-025formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep165_necessityWitness_extends_fep025_current

fep-166fep-160formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep166_splitUnique_extends_fep160_aoNess
The competing-pair uniqueness of the law-weighted split is paired with fep-160's unconditional existence decomposition, so on the same finite rate-field carrier the canonical split exists and any constraint-satisfying competitor coincides with it, without introducing a stationarity hypothesis or a nonnegativity claim for the circulation part.
fep-167fep-162formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep167_frobeniusProjection_extends_fep162_clairautSymmetrize
The Frobenius least-squares projection layer is paired with fep-162's algebraic symmetrization construction, so the constructed discrete Hessian is exactly the unique symmetric minimizer, without claiming a continuum Clairaut theorem or a general Bregman-projection existence result.
fep-168fep-163formal_pairingFEPComposed.fep168_remainderBound_extends_fep163_solenoidalExpansion
The quantitative remainder budget is paired with fep-163's exact three-term expansion, so the uncanceled divergence remainder is bounded and its equality case attained instead of being assumed to vanish, without an unconditional-drop claim.

Support controls the direction of KL convergence

pε=(1−ε,ε), δ=(1,0); 0<ε≤0.1. Endpoint ε=0 has both KL values zero.

TV(pε,δ)=ε; KL(δ||pε)=−log(1−ε); KL(pε||δ)=+∞ for every ε>0.

Native extended-real KL; null means +∞, never a plotted finite replacement. TV convergence does not imply KL convergence in both directions.
